🪶 Backstory Generator

"Tragic past? Check. Mysterious secret? Check. Living relatives? Unlikely."

Roll a character's personality and past: two traits, an ideal, a bond, a flaw, where they grew up, their family, a mentor and a rival by name, the turning points of their life, why they took up adventuring, a secret, and hooks the DM can pull on. Keep the lines you like, reroll the rest, and save it to a character in the Character Builder.

The backstory lives in the address bar, so 🔗 Copy Link shares it and a reload keeps it; nothing else is saved. 🧝 Use for My Character adds it to the end of a character's notes in the Character Builder (and gives it this name if it has none), saved in this browser (💾 back up everything).
The race and class names are from the System Reference Document 5.1 by Wizards of the Coast LLC, licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License. The tables are the Gazette's own.

How to use a rolled backstory

A 5e character's personality comes in four parts: personality traits (how they act at the table, usually two), an ideal (what they believe in), a bond (who or what they'd fight for), and a flaw (what gets them into trouble). The generator rolls those, then adds the past that explains them: where they grew up, their family, the mentor who taught them and the rival who won't let them go (both by name), three turning points by age, why they left to adventure, the secret they keep, and a hook the DM can use to bring that past back into the story. The last line, For the DM, names the mentor or rival in a scene ready to run.

Keep, reroll, and mix

  • 🔒 Keep a line and 🎲 Roll New Backstory leaves it alone while everything else changes.
  • 🎲 on a single line rerolls only that line.
  • Pick a race for names from that people and a chance of an upbringing that fits them. Pick a class for a chance of a reason to adventure, a secret, and a mentor's lesson that fit it: a paladin's oath, a warlock's patron, a wizard's missing spellbook. Pick a background (soldier, sage, urchin, and ten more) for a chance of an upbringing, a reason, a secret, and a mentor from that walk of life. Turning-point ages follow the race, so an elf's childhood runs long.

Treat the result as a first draft. Two lines that seem to clash often make the best character: a cheerful trait with a grim secret, or a bond to a family the character claims to hate. Rewrite anything that doesn't fit, and talk the secret and the hook over with your DM before the first session, so they show up in the story and not only on your sheet.

Works with

🧝 Use for My Character writes the backstory into the notes of a character in the Character Builder, or starts a new one with this race, class, and name. Work out the scores first in the Point Buy Calculator. DMs who need a whole cast of side characters can roll them in Town Square, which shares the trait, ideal, bond, and flaw tables.
